
# Conformance (Clause)

`ogc.api.processes.part1.v1.clauses.conformance` *v1.0*

## Description

<!-- Generated by scripts/extract_part1_v1.py; source SHA-256 1a1dcb80556dc054440fab25ef73c1535549c19e9e327877cf1c17f65007d32d. -->

<p class="source-citation"><a href="https://docs.ogc.org/is/18-062r2/18-062r2.html#toc9">Published source: OGC 18-062r2, 1.0.0 (toc9)</a>.</p>

<div id="sc_conformance">
<span id="toc9"></span>
<p id="_8e58c6d7-d142-9ef5-199d-6cb77dafd205">This standard defines seven requirements / conformance classes.</p>
<p id="_878d098f-a27e-13d5-6f4d-16bb65202c37">The standardization targets of all conformance classes are “Web APIs.”</p>
<p id="_ca35a6f6-9a74-be85-5933-91630bc92e0f">The main requirements class is:</p>
<ul id="_1af9da05-8dd3-5b17-fd71-43f981f0c351">
<li>
<p id="_1aece7e2-60d0-8105-7064-a2a555df8359"><a href="#rc_core">Core</a>.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p id="_6cb652ca-da8b-317e-c5b6-a433d61f3467">The <i>Core</i> specifies requirements that all Web APIs have to implement.</p>
<p id="_f57b4ed1-f8db-9328-445f-41b258771a88">Two requirements classes depend on the <i>Core</i> and specify representations for the resources specified in the <i>Core</i>:</p>
<ul id="_061e9fbd-d8c0-6f8c-b944-7139f20867a9">
<li>
<p id="_124a2e2c-1ef4-7412-9ead-c9ed58bfbfac"><a href="#rc_json">JSON</a>, and</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_fe10adf1-9eec-9541-7bcf-69ed71f493a3"><a href="#rc_html">HTML</a>.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p id="_6860fc94-956d-5894-4ce8-7cf375e82627">The JSON encoding is mandatory.</p>
<p id="_92c6ceee-57b1-eb6d-d316-20fd1c348352">The <i>Core</i> does not mandate any encoding or format for the formal definition of the API. OpenAPI 3.0 specification is one option for defining the Processing API. As such a requirements class has been specified for OpenAPI 3.0, which depends on the requirements class <i>Core</i>:</p>
<ul id="_11cc3c95-dc6d-6543-371f-377c94564a34">
<li>
<p id="_f0810e5d-5dd4-a1b0-ac0d-48547f036b22"><a href="#rc_oas30">OpenAPI Specification 3.0</a>.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p id="_0e3b3357-6802-a191-1a20-8b877459d825">An implementation of the <i>Core</i> requirements class may also decide to use other API definition representations in addition to, or instead of, an OpenAPI 3.0 definition. Examples for alternative API definitions: OpenAPI 2.0 (Swagger), future versions of the OpenAPI specification, an OWS Common 2.0 capabilities document or WSDL.<div class="Note" id="_5259e05f-d315-259c-4757-c8186c05a32a"><p><span class="note_label">NOTE</span>  OpenAPI 3.0 offers an open, powerful and vendor neutral description format.
While the use of OpenAPI 3.0 for the formal definition of the API is not mandatory, the requests/responses of the API specified in this standard are defined using OpenAPI 3.0 schemas.
See also the note regarding <a href="#req_core_landingpage-success">/req/core/landingpage-success</a></p></div></p>
<p id="_d92cad4c-992d-14b6-20b0-7802cf248ea8">The <i>Core</i> is intended to be a minimal useful API for the execution of processes in the geospatial domain. The Core is designed to map the operations of a Web Processing Service 2.0 instance.</p>
<p id="_a7a05a1b-6e1d-c001-c12b-71e3c2703459">The <i>Core</i> does not mandate the use of any specific process description to
specify the interface of a process. Instead this standard defines and
recommends the use of the following conformance class:</p>
<ul id="_06f9c46c-0d92-aff6-52b7-c3791e378c3a">
<li>
<p id="_a5865a8d-7733-87e1-a81a-29bf2c67be99">
<a href="#rc_ogc-process-description">OGC Process Description</a>
</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p id="_a9c4c408-ca42-d8a0-6751-a63a6feef88e">This class defines an information model, encoded in JSON, which may be used to
specify the interface of a process.</p>
<p id="_a352eca5-a5ee-e3c3-e1c6-fca12e736fbe">Three additional conformance classes are specified that extend the basic functionality of an API:</p>
<ul id="_8b588bc2-3323-74ac-db73-f20b6d2d262b">
<li>
<p id="_c0a50caf-dc6e-e4de-a340-8e0aad58c9d5"><a href="#rc_job-list">Job list</a>, and</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_be2bf791-7306-e570-aecd-7276c0a6393c"><a href="#rc_callback">Callback</a>, and</p>
</li>
<li>
<p id="_b9654c6d-cd70-f220-116b-5ad0c3ee8bbd"><a href="#rc_dismiss">Dismiss</a>.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p id="_2b5aea31-6778-4909-07c9-7739738e652f">Additional capabilities such as support for transactions, extended job monitoring, etc., may be specified in future parts of the OGC API — Processes series or as vendor-specific extensions.</p>
<p id="_19ea86de-0ea0-2b61-8ca7-0bde4fdf1562">Conformance with this standard SHALL be checked using all the relevant tests specified in Annex A (normative) of this document. The framework, concepts, and methodology for testing, and the criteria to be achieved to claim conformance are specified in the OGC Compliance Testing Policies and Procedures and the OGC Compliance Testing web site.</p>
